The paper proposes BladeNet, a dual-module CNN architecture for detecting surface faults on composite wind turbine blades using drone imagery.
BladeNet first performs unsupervised blade detection and extraction using a U-Net instance segmentation model.
BladeNet then applies semi-supervised anomaly detection methods like VAE, AnoGAN, GANomaly, Skip-GANomaly, and PANDA to the extracted blade regions to identify anomalous areas.
The PANDA semi-supervised anomaly detection method achieves the highest AUC of 0.639 on the Ørsted turbine blade dataset.
BladeNet outperforms other object detection methods like Mask R-CNN, YOLACT, and Cascade Mask R-CNN, achieving an AP of 0.995 on the Ørsted dataset and 0.223 on the DTU NordTank dataset.
BladeNet's blade detection masks closely fit the turbine blades, including accurately capturing the sharp triangular parts, unlike other methods.
The Ørsted dataset contains 2637 high-resolution drone images of offshore wind turbines, while the DTU NordTank dataset has 1170 images of onshore turbines.
Automating wind turbine blade inspection is crucial to aid engineers in monitoring blade health across the large number of blades in modern wind farms.
Semi-supervised anomaly detection is important for this application as it is impossible to account for all possible forms of blade defects a priori.
BladeNet introduces negative image samples of sky and ground during training to help the model focus on the turbine blades and ignore background clutter.
The U-Net architecture used for blade detection allows BladeNet to produce high-resolution instance segmentation masks that closely fit the blade edges.
BladeNet's dual-stage approach of first extracting the blades and then applying semi-supervised anomaly detection is key to its performance.
The paper evaluates multiple semi-supervised anomaly detection algorithms to determine the best fit for the wind turbine blade application.
Accurate blade detection and extraction is critical for the subsequent semi-supervised anomaly detection stage to work effectively.
The paper demonstrates BladeNet's robustness by training on the Ørsted dataset and transferring to the DTU NordTank dataset with high performance.
